title: What are the largest and smallest numbers with exactly thirty presses?
description: Creative Chitti makes nine hundred ninety seven in twenty five presses. The video finds another number of presses for it, and then the largest and smallest three digit numbers that need exactly thirty presses. Keeko raises a hand, thinking that the largest is nine hundred ninety nine.
teaching_notes: One idea: the fewest presses of a number is its digit sum, and each trade of one press for ten smaller presses adds nine presses. Ask the class what the digit sum of nine hundred ninety seven is before any trade. Watch for students who pick the number with the biggest digits without checking its presses.

source: (a) You have to make exactly 30 button presses. What is the largest 3-digit number you can make? What is the smallest 3-digit number you can make? (b) 997 can be made using 25 clicks. Can you make 997 with a different number of clicks?
video_script.why: The child can make a number by trading one big press for ten smaller presses.
video_script.substitution: The fewest presses of a number is its digit sum, and each trade of one press for ten smaller presses adds nine presses.
video_script.anchor: With exactly thirty presses, which is the largest three digit number and which is the smallest?
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko picks 999 because nines are the biggest digits. But 999 takes 9 + 9 + 9 = 27 presses, and each trade adds nine, so its counts are 27 then 36, never 30.
video_script.payoff_line: With exactly thirty presses, the largest is nine hundred ninety three and the smallest is one hundred two

final_answer.value: 997 in 34 presses too; largest 993 and smallest 102 with exactly 30 presses
final_answer.spoken: the largest is nine hundred ninety three and the smallest is one hundred two

maths_rules: each trade adds 9 presses, so presses = digit sum + 9 × trades
30 = digit sum + 9 × trades; the digit sum of a 3-digit number is at most 27, so the digit sum is 21, 12 or 3
largest 3-digit number with digit sum 21 is 993: (8 × 100) + (19 × 10) + (3 × 1) is 8 + 19 + 3 = 30 presses
smallest 3-digit number with digit sum 3 is 102: (8 × 10) + (22 × 1) is 8 + 22 = 30 presses
the slip: 999 takes 27 presses or 36, never 30
video_script.design: One idea: presses are the digit sum plus nine for every trade. Wrong idea: Keeko picks the number with the biggest digits. The anchor stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part; no hard clear.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The fewest presses for a number is the sum of its digits, called the digit sum.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>For nine hundred ninety seven, nine plus nine plus seven is twenty five presses.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, trade a press of the hundred button for ten presses of the ten button.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Nine hundred ninety seven becomes eight hundreds, nineteen tens and seven ones.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>That takes eight, nineteen and seven presses, which is thirty four. It is nine more than before.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: each trade adds 9 presses; digit sum + 9 × trades = 30; the digit sum is 21, 12 or 3

marks.m1: each trade is marked with plus 9
marks.m3: 21, 12 and 3 are written as the possible digit sums

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, each trade adds nine presses to the digit sum.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>For exactly thirty presses, the digit sum plus nine times the trades must be thirty.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The biggest digit sum for three digits is twenty seven. That leaves a digit sum of twenty one, twelve, or three.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>For digit sum twenty one, put nines in the hundreds and tens places, leaving three. The largest number is nine hundred ninety three.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Trade a hundred for ten tens to get eight, nineteen and three, which is exactly thirty presses.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The smallest number has digit sum three, and that is one hundred two.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Trade the hundred for ten tens, then two tens for twenty ones. That gives eight tens and twenty two ones, which is thirty presses.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>With exactly thirty presses, the largest is nine hundred ninety three and the smallest is one hundred two.
